Mala Bahachivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mala Bahachivka, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery appears on an 1860s Russian topographic map, suggesting it was established soon after the colony's founding, and again on a 1941 map; it was likely demolished during the postwar Soviet period, with locals recalling bulldozing and tombstones taken away or buried in the forest. Bogachevka (the village's name before 1945) was founded as a Jewish agricultural colony in 1850 by settlers from Podolia and Volyn - 418 people across 84 families, each receiving at least two of 146 total land plots. Population reached 671 by 1869; many colonists worked in domestic crafts and petty trade, though by 1870 only 2 of 40 farming families cultivated with their own equipment and animals. Population was entirely Jewish (506 people) by 1897, supporting a synagogue and heder. Civil War-era robbery gangs pillaged the community; a Yiddish elementary school operated in 1925, though population fell to 326 (13%) by 1926 as youth migrated to cities. A 1929 kolkhoz, Pyatrychka, followed. Romanian occupation from August 1941 found many residents already evacuated or mobilized; the remaining 131 Jews were murdered that autumn. Nearly a dozen Jewish families returned after 1945, but the village is now practically (and likely formally) non-existent - locals say only one person lives there today.
